reviews.title: The best food tracking app
reviews.text: I’ve used the more well-known food tracker for 14 years on and off, and I’d been increasingly dissatisfied with it. When I found Nutracheck I can’t believe how much more useful, convenient, and accurate it is! The price of a one year subscription is 1/3 that of the other app. The food database is much larger and more accurate. The other app had so many useless amounts, like “one fillet of cod”; is that 3 oz. or 12 oz?  I love having the barcode scanning feature while still paying a reasonable price. I needed about 3 days to get aquatinted with how this app worked, but it wasn’t difficult to learn. I really love Nutracheck!

reviews.text: let me first start by saying that this app is fairly well laid out I like the clean user interface I like the little micro trackers for water and fruit and vegetable intake. I think that’s pretty awesome. I also like that there’s a pretty solid database which a lot of these apps don’t have, but I was surprised to find that the only wearables that were available for integration were Garmin and Fitbit, especially considering it’s touting about being one of the number one Apple store apps, but it doesn’t integrate with Apple health or Apple Watch so that’s crazy unless there’s something I’m missing in the features so developers if that’s the case, please hit me up and let me know.

reviews.title: Great App, Use Daily
reviews.text:
I was diagnosed with Diabetes 5 years ago and was having a rough time changing my diet.  This app was instrumental in my success.  Not only is there an extensive database of food items. You can include your own items/recipes (even making adjusting your recipes easier).  

So not only can I easily track calories, but salt, sugar, protein, fat, etc., but I can plan ahead reducing grocery costs because now I’m reducing waste by only buying what I need (less spoilage).  You can even track activities which can lead to increased food amounts.

This app is essential in my success, by using it I’ve maintained an A1C of 5.2 for 4 years.

Would rate higher if I could!
